newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up slightly despite meeting.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up slightly despite meeting.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B index closed up slightly in cautious trading on Friday despite a meeting to discuss ways to keep domestic investors out of the B share market, brokers said.
Market regulators and major securities houses met in Shanghai on Friday to discuss ways to curb domestic investors trading on the B share market, which is intended for foreigners, they said.
The B share index gained 0.449 points or 0.59 percent to 76.225 points on volume of 11.647 million shares worth $7.773 million.

In spite of the minor rebound on Friday, sentiment remained weak after the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule at midnight on Monday, which removed a major positive factor from the market, brokers said.
"The slight gain in the B share market was just a technical rebound, and the future trend is still uncertain," said one broker.
The regulatory meeting, which focused on implementation of existing rules banning domestic investors from trading in the B share market, may have affected sentiment, brokers said.
But no new control measures for B share trading were discussed at the meeting, they said.
"If the meeting works out some solid new measures to ban domestic investors from trading B shares, it would have had a negative impact on the market," a local broker said.
But China has already banned local investors from the B share market and Friday's meeting had little impact on trading as it was viewed as a way to improve lax enforcement, brokers said.
"In China, there is always lax enforcement in imposing government policies," the local broker said. "So I do not think the meeting could really shake the B share market."
Of 45 B shares, 39 traded with 19 up, 12 down and eight flat.
Shanghai Yaohua Pilkington Glass Co was the best performer, jumping $0.034 or 9.29 percent to $0.400 on volume of 99,500 shares.
Recently-listed Hainan Airlines Co was the most actively traded on domestic buying. It gained $0.010 or 1.92 percent to $0.530 on volume of 1.5 million shares.
Shanghai's domestic currency A share index also saw a technical rebound due to a burst of selective buying late in the afternoon session, brokers said.
The A index gained 9.164 points or 0.76 percent to 1,211.447 points on volume of 423.133 million shares worth 5.0 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index added 26.710 points or 0.70 percent to 3,823.668 points.
Brokers said the A and B share markets could test lower next week due to continued weak sentiment.
"Any rebound will be limited," said one broker. "The technical picture still points towards a downward track."
